name: Connacht

attributes.attribute: a great legendary king of Tara
cried out when Conn drew near
born in the reign of Conn

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The entry gathers the story of Conn of the Hundred Battles. Among the great kings of legend in Ireland, Conn stood out. The magic stone Lia Fail announced him, crying out each time he drew near. He proved the rightful king by walking the ramparts of Tara daily. Before that he ruled the northern part of Ireland, while his rival Eogan Mor held the South, the two lands split by the glacial hill line of the Eiscir Riada. Conn crossed into his rival's territory and beat him. Eogan bear, returned with aid, and died in a second clash at Mag Lena. These wars won him his title among the fiercest knights of legend. The land stayed fruitful so long as a loyal king ruled it. He wed the good Eithna, under whom the fields gave three crops. When he took Be Chuma, a woman bound out of the Otherworld, no cow gave milk until she left. The hero Finno was born while he reigned, and though Conn killed Fionn's father, he kept a friendship with Fionn.

okr.objective: The record retells the reign of king Conn of the Hundreds.
key_results: Conn was the first to pass the special stone at Tara.
He fought Eogan Mor and won the battle of Magenna.
The land gave three crops under his good rule.
He was said to be the one who killed the father of Fionn.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
